description: Mars 2020 landing hardware on the surface, as HiRISE imaged it on 19 Feb 2021 (the day after landing). Positions measured for the game's landing mission.

image.product: ESP_068294_1985_RED.abrowse.jpg (map-projected browse of the RED RDR, north up, 2048 px wide = 30044 RDR samples, 3.67 m/px; checked against its 500 m scale bar: 136 px)
image.label: ESP_068294_1985_RED.LBL (equirectangular, MAP_SCALE 0.25 m, CENTER_LATITUDE 15°, A_AXIS_RADIUS 3394.84 km)
image.identification: https://uahirise.org/releases/perseverance/m2020-hardware-labels.jpg (HiRISE team's annotated frame), matched to the browse with two craters as control points

method: The rover is the anchor: its position is Perseverance's first logged waypoint (MMGIS, sol 13; data/build/rover/rover.json), so the hardware keeps its offsets from the rover even where the RDR's absolute registration differs from the MMGIS base map. Each object's offset in browse pixels is converted with the label's projection (east-west 3.603 m/px, north-south 3.669 m/px at this latitude). Uncertainty about one browse pixel (±4 m) per axis, plus the anchor's own.

rover.basis: MMGIS waypoint, sol 13 (before the first drive, sol 14)

crossChecks: NASA: the parachute and backshell lie about 1 km northwest of the landing site (science.nasa.gov/missions/mars-2020-perseverance/images-of-edl-debris/); measured 1.15 km at 293°.
NASA/JPL PIA24333: the descent stage's debris forms a V pointing back toward the rover; measured 0.70 km NW, on that line.
